title: Turning Fails into Features: Zapier’s Hard-Won Eval Lessons — Rafal Willinski, Vitor Balocco, Zapier
talk_summary: Zapier's agent team describes building a data flywheel from instrumented traces to evals, warning that unit-test-style evals overfit to one model's path and that trajectory/LLM-judge/rubric evals plus staged A/B rollouts are needed to compare models fairly. They also show how to mine implicit feedback (copying responses, rephrasing, cursing) and use reasoning models over traces to find root causes and explain model differences.

takeaways.what_they_do: Log runs in the same shape as runtime (tool calls, errors, pre/post-processing) so any interesting trace can be turned into an eval with prepopulated inputs and expected outputs, ideally one click.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there should be like a one click to turn it into an eval. It should become your instinct.

takeaways.technique: Trajectory evals instead of only unit assertions
takeaways.what_they_do: Let the agent run to the end state and grade all tool calls and artifacts along the way, not just the next action, because unit evals penalize valid alternative paths.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we are not grading just the end state but we are also grading all the tool calls that were made along the way

takeaways.technique: Reasoning-model diff of two models' traces
takeaways.what_they_do: Feed traces from two candidate models to a reasoning LLM and ask what is actually different, surfacing behavioral traits (decisive vs. chatty, bad JSON) that aggregate scores hide.
takeaways.evidence_quote: look at this run, look at this run and tell me what's actually different about the new model

takeaways.technique: Rubric-based LLM judging with per-case rubrics
takeaways.what_they_do: Each eval row carries human-written natural-language rubrics telling the judge what to attend to, e.g. whether the agent retried after an unexpected API error.
takeaways.evidence_quote: each row in our data set has a different set of rubrics, rubrics that were handcrafted by a human

takeaways.technique: Cluster failures into an automatic roadmap
takeaways.what_they_do: Aggregate and cluster feedback and failure modes at scale to see which tools and interactions fail most, producing a prioritized improvement list.

takeaways.technique: Split regression vs. aspirational eval pools
takeaways.what_they_do: Maintain one dataset guarding existing behavior against regressions and a separate set of extremely hard aspirational cases, and treat near-100% pass as a sign the set is uninteresting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: dividing the data set into two pools... the regressions data set... and also the aspirational data set
